frequency_question: How often do executive agency principals follow through on terminating a major recognized professional gatekeeper's status when intent is signaled within a fixed window?
membership_rule: Federal executive department actions targeting national professional association recognition; excludes routine renewals or voluntary relinquishments.

cases.name: US Department of Education removal of ACICS recognition (First instance 2016)
US Department of Education removal of ACICS recognition (Second instance / final death blow 2022)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named terminal deregistration actions executed by the Department of Education against major accrediting bodies in recent decades.
known_gaps: Small sample size because total revocation of a dominant professional monopoly gatekeeper is exceptionally rare.
skeleton: Total high-stakes recognized accreditor termination attempts by the Department of Education where the principal agency leadership actively drove the revocation against the entity's will over the last 15 years.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 2 major ideologically/politically driven departmental challenges against dominant national accreditors equals 100 percent historical follow-through rate among initiated terminal reviews.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to the institutional behavior of federal education administrative principals, which remains stable across modern political cycles.
